lines.text: Job calls his friends miserable comforters and says he would use his mouth to encourage them.
Job says God has devastated all his cities, shattered him while he was at ease, and crushed him.
Job has sewn sackcloth over his skin, and says his hands are free of violence and his prayer pure.
Job says his witness is at the city gate, and that his friends are his scoffers.
Job pictures Sheol as home, calls corruption his father and the worm his mother, then asks where his hope is.
